description: Challenge A2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Plaid has the /æ/ vowel. Played has /eɪ/, plead has /i/, and plied has /aɪ/.
Swept has the short /ɛ/ vowel and ends with the /pt/ cluster. Slept and wept have /ɛ/ but begin differently; sweat ends with /t/ without the /p/ sound.
Rough has /ʌ/ in General American. Roof has /u/ or /ʊ/ depending on speaker, rouge has /uːʒ/, and row has /oʊ/.
Sugar begins with /ʃ/. Supper and singer begin with /s/, while shiver also begins with /ʃ/ but has a different vowel and ending.
Quick begins with /kw/. Wick begins with /w/, while kick and sick begin with /k/ and /s/.
Thief begins with /θ/. Chief begins with /tʃ/, sheaf with /ʃ/, and leaf with /l/.
Breath ends with unvoiced /θ/. Bread ends with /d/, breed with /d/, and breathe ends with voiced /ð/.
Months ends with the /θs/ cluster. Month ends with /θ/, monk with /ŋk/, and moss with /s/.
Asked ends with /t/ after the /s/ sound. Ask has no final /t/, asks ends with /s/, and acting ends with /ŋ/.
Enough uses gh to spell the final /f/ sound. Tough ends with the same /f/ but has a different vowel; though and through have different vowel sounds and final sounds.
Island has a silent s and is pronounced /ˈaɪlənd/. Isle and islet are different words; Ireland has a different ending and stress pattern.
Knuckle begins with /n/ because the k is silent. Nickel also begins with /n/ but has /ɪ/ rather than /ʌ/; noble and needle have different vowel and syllable patterns.
